subject: Renewal conversation — upgrade pathway from eight to sixteen GPU reserved pool
participants_external: james.carter@vectorai.io (James Carter, Head of ML Ops)
messages:
From: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@vectorai.io>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@vectorai.io, james.carter@vectorai.io
Date: 2027-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning & capacity request

Sean —

We’re starting our renewal planning for the Dedicated pool and wanted to surface that our engineering leads are asking whether we can move from our current 8-GPU reserved pool to 16 GPUs for the next 12-month commit. Over the past quarter our production p50 latency has held, but peak throughput is constraining a new batch of experiments.

Attached is our quarter usage export for your reference (vectorai_usage_Q3.csv). High-level asks:
- Pricing for a straight x2 commit with monthly committed GPUs and any volume discounts
- Expected activation lead time and staged ramp options (we'd prefer a phased activation to validate ops)
- Throughput guarantees or fallback behaviors if we burst beyond committed throughput (we rely on predictable capacity for user-facing features)

Can we set up a short call this week to run through options?

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Moreno
VP of Engineering, VectorAI
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@vectorai.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning & capacity request

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the heads up and the usage file. I reviewed the Q3 export and it lines up with a predictable steady baseline plus several short high-concurrency windows. We can absolutely support a 16-GPU reserved pool for the renewal term. A few quick notes before the call so we make the time efficient:

1) Pricing model: we’ll prepare two options — a straight committed-month model (flat monthly fee for 16 GPUs) and a phased-activation model (8 committed + option to turn on additional 8 at a discounted incremental rate during business hours). Marissa will lead the line items.

2) Activation timing: standard lead time to fully provision 16 GPUs in a Dedicated pool is ~10 business days after amendment execution for the region you’ve been using (us-west-2). We can do a staged activation over 2–3 days to move traffic gradually.

3) Throughput and fallbacks: we propose an SLA addendum that includes throughput guardrails—if observed 1-minute token QPS exceeds committed pool capacity, requests will either be queued (up to a short tolerable window) or routed to a compatible model variant in our burst tier (with clear cost/latency tradeoffs). We’ll attach a doc with the proposed decision tree.

Can you do 30 minutes Thursday 11/4 at 11am PT? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and Marissa will bring the pricing scenarios.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@vectorai.io>, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-11-03T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Draft commercial options for VectorAI renewal (8 -> 16 GPUs)

Alice / Team —

Following Sean’s note, attached is a concise two-option commercial proposal (proposed_amendment_8_to_16_v1.pdf). Highlights:

Option A — Direct upgrade (single amendment)
- 16 GPU monthly committed pool, 12-month term
- Unit pricing: $X,XXX per GPU / month (flat)
- 10% multi-month discount for early renewal sign-off
- SLA: 99.95% pool availability; throughput guardrails doc attached

Option B — Phased activation (lower near-term spend)
- Base commit: 8 GPUs monthly + optional secondary 8 GPUs in a reserved burst configuration
- Secondary GPUs billed at 70% of base unit price while in burst mode
- Staged activation timeline and ops runbook included

Key operational items:
- Activation window: 10 business days for full provisioning, 48–72 hours for staged ramp steps
- We’ll run a short pre-cutover soak test with traffic mirroring for 24 hours
- Change control and rollback plan included in throughput_guardrails.docx

If you want, Mina from CS can coordinate a playbook run-through and ensure our SRE team pairs with your ML Ops team on cutover.

Next step: confirm whether you prefer Option A or B and any additional procurement constraints (purchase order, invoice cadence, SOW).

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_amendment_8_to_16_v1.pdf

Date: 2027-11-05T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft commercial options for VectorAI renewal (8 -> 16 GPUs)

Marissa / Sean —

Thanks for the clear options. A couple of technical clarifications from our ML Ops side before we move toward procurement:

- Can you lock p99 latency for inference traffic routed to the primary pool or do burst routes have variable tail-latency? We need tight tail bounds for the customer-facing API.
- For the phased model, will KV cache warmup be transferred automatically when adding the second block of GPUs? If not, what warmup window should we plan for?
- During the 24-hour soak, what telemetry will be available to our team (token-level breakdown, per-node CPU/GPU utilization, and request traces)?

Also, procurement asked about the amendment format — we need a single signed amendment that references the existing master agreement and a simple schedule for billing. If you can attach a redline-friendly amendment we’ll take it to legal.

Thanks,
James Carter
Head of ML Ops, VectorAI
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: James Carter <james.carter@vectorai.io>, alice.moreno@vectorai.io
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, procurement@vectorai.io
Date: 2027-11-07T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft commercial options for VectorAI renewal (8 -> 16 GPUs)

James —

Great questions — answering inline:  
- p99 latency: the primary pool SLA covers availability and a tested p99 baseline for the pinned model family. For burst-routed requests to fallback variants, we can publish an expected p99 range and commit to routing policies that prefer queued short waits over routing to higher-latency variants when configured. We’ll include measured p99 numbers from comparable customers in the amendment appendix.
- KV cache warmup: cache migration is not automatic across model shards. Our recommended approach is a short mirrored warmup (48 hours) with targeted mirroring of hot prefixes during the staged activation; we’ll provide a script and runbook. Expect a transient throughput delta during warmup which we quantify in the runbook.
- Telemetry during soak: we’ll provide token-level QPS, per-node GPU utilization, tail-latency traces, and an access link to a live dashboard for the soak window. Full traces will be available for 30 days by default (we can extend retention as an add-on).

Attached: throughput_guardrails.docx (decision tree + rollback), and a redline-friendly amendment draft will be uploaded to the shared drive by EOD (link: https://drive.redwood.com/docs/RDW-6279-proposed-amendment).

If VectorAI is comfortable with Option B (phased activation) we can issue the amendment with staged billing and a DocuSign link for procurement. Marissa — I’ll leave pricing finalization and the DocuSign to you.

Best,
Sean
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: throughput_guardrails.docx
